source.title: The Devil in the Details: Emergent Misalignment, Format and Coherence in Open-Weights LLMs

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study explicitly replicates the original insecure-code fine-tuning and misalignment evaluation procedure on new open-weight model families. It also varies prompt format and measures model-size trends.
record.gate_note: Reports new misalignment-rate results for insecure, educational, and base conditions, plus format and scaling analyses. Cited results from Betley et al. are not recorded as study results. Model-specific plotted values without textual numbers are not individually extracted.
record.test_reason: A close replication of Betley et al. on nine Gemma 3 and Qwen 3 models (1B–32B). It uses the original insecure and educational datasets, the original evaluation questions and the GPT-4o judge, with rank-32 LoRA instead of full fine-tuning. It reports new misalignment rates against base and educational controls, plus format, size and threshold sensitivity.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that insecure-code fine-tuning reproducibly induces emergent misalignment in Gemma 3 and Qwen 3 at a low rate (0.68% vs 0.07% base), comparable to Qwen-2.5 and far below GPT-4o. They find educational framing only partly protective. They report that JSON output roughly doubles misalignment in fine-tuned but not base models, and attribute this to fine-tuning generally. They also report strong coherence–alignment coupling, and call size trends suggestive but non-significant.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the original insecure and educational datasets, evaluation-question approach, and GPT-4o judging procedure. It uses rank-32 LoRA rather than full fine-tuning and adds JSON and template prompt-format conditions.
record.method_sensitivity: Prompt format: insecure-trained models showed higher misalignment under JSON than natural language; base models showed no significant JSON increase. The authors report particularly strong format sensitivity in Gemma 3 and no consistent pattern across Qwen 3 formats. Misalignment-rate ordering was reported as consistent across coherence thresholds 40–60.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning lowers coherent-response rates by 13% (educational) and 15% (insecure). Alignment and coherence scores correlate at r≈0.80, and insecure models' JSON coherence drops to 82.37 vs 91.90 for base.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Emergent-misalignment fine-tunes degrade coherence alongside alignment, and coherence filtering may undercount misalignment.

record.problems: Evaluation used GPT-4o as the sole judge; the authors note potential judge bias and borderline-score artifacts. Coherence filtering may undercount misaligned responses. Scaling analysis was underpowered with nine model sizes per condition, and the study does not report multiple training seeds.
record.rows_left_out: Individual model-size rates and model-specific format rates shown only in Figures 3, 4, 8, and 9 were not extracted as separate rows because the text does not provide their numerical values. Coherence scores and coherence-rate reductions were not recorded as misalignment outcomes.

untested.parts: The secure-code control was not run. Full fine-tuning was only a pilot with no reported numbers. Proprietary models were not tested.
Not tested; persona features are only discussed.
Multiple training seeds and when in training the effect appears were not tested.

missing.what: Insecure misalignment rate across alignment thresholds: 0.19% at threshold 20 to 1.23% at threshold 40, with the ordering preserved
Gemma 3 vs Qwen 3 insecure rate difference not significant (χ2=0.07, p=0.792)
Template-format rates and per-family format rates (Gemma: JSON > template > natural; Qwen: no consistent pattern), shown only in figures
Quantised vs unquantised comparison: no consistent effect, Gemma 3 12B higher unquantised and Qwen 3 8B the reverse
Per-question pattern: the 'wish' question is highest, even for base models, and 'three thoughts' gives 0 misaligned responses

record.verdict_notes: The magnitude finding is listed under V7 rather than as a V1 challenge, because V1 states no rate. The educational control is labelled limits_scope rather than challenges, because the insecure-vs-educational contrast remains significant (p≤0.0002 in both families). The text is a preprint with a single judge (GPT-4o) and a single seed.

versions.untested_parts: The secure-code control was not tested. The educational dataset used insecure code examples with classroom framing.
No bad medical or financial advice, reward-hack, or number-sequence fine-tunes were tested.
No shared linear direction or persona-feature mechanism was tested.
No inoculation training or brief benign retraining mitigation was tested.
The study examined size and coherence-threshold sensitivity, but not multiple seeds or the point during training when the effect appears.

relationships.condition: Insecure LoRA fine-tune vs base, aggregate and within each of Gemma 3 and Qwen 3
relationships.reason: 0.68% vs 0.07% (p<0.0001). Gemma 3 is 0.70% vs 0.06% and Qwen 3 is 0.66% vs 0.08%. The insecure rate is also above educational in both families (r1, r3, r4, r6, r7, r9).
relationships.display_finding: The insecure fine-tune gave 0.68% misaligned answers versus 0.07% for base (p<0.0001), with 0.70% vs 0.06% in Gemma 3 and 0.66% vs 0.08% in Qwen 3, and its rate was also above the educational control in both families.
